Zesty Cowboy Butter Recipe

(
0
REVIEWS)

Instaread
Cowboy butter is a loaded compound butter with garlic, herbs, lemon, Dijon, a little heat, and a savory kick from Worcestershire, perfect compound butter for any grilling dish!!!
PREP:
5 minutes mins
TOTAL:
SERVES:
8
JUMP TO RECIPE

Steak night is already doing most of the work. But if you want it to taste like you had a steakhouse hiding in the backyard, this cowboy butter recipe the only way you’ll do steak!

It’s softened butter loaded with fresh herbs, garlic, Dijon, lemon juice, lemon zest, red pepper flakes, and a little horseradish for bite. Mix it, chill it, slice it, and drop it onto hot steak, burgers, grilled chicken, potatoes, or crusty bread.

You get about 1 cup of flavorful compound butter, and the active work is 10 minutes. The fridge handles the rest.

And you’ll want to keep this in stock at all times. Once the family gets a taste, it will be constantly requested.. trust me!

How to Make Zesty Cowboy Butter

Soften the butter, mix in the remaining ingredients, then chill it into a log so you can slice rounds onto hot food. The key is using softened butter, not melted butter, so the butter mixture stays creamy and holds its shape.

1

Soften the Butter

  • Let it sit: Use 1 cup unsalted butter and let it soften at room temperature until you can mash it with a fork.
  • Don’t melt it: Melted butter gets greasy and won’t roll cleanly into the shape of a log.
2

Mix the Cowboy Butter

  • Add the bite: Stir in 2 tablespoons prepared horseradish, drained if it looks watery. That’s Derek’s steakhouse-style twist.
  • Build the flavor: Add fresh parsley, fresh chives, Dijon mustard, lemon juice, lemon zest, fresh garlic, Worcestershire sauce, smoked paprika, kosher salt, black pepper, red pepper flakes, and a pinch of cayenne if you want more heat.
  • Mix it well: Use a fork or rubber spatula in a medium bowl and scrape the sides so there aren’t plain butter pockets hiding in there.
3

Taste, Roll, and Chill

  • Taste first: Add more salt for depth, more lemon for brightness, more red pepper flakes for heat, or a little extra horseradish if you want it sharper.
  • Roll it up: Spoon the butter onto parchment paper or plastic wrap, roll it into a log, and twist the ends tight.
  • Chill until firm: Give it about 1 hour in the fridge so it slices clean and melts slowly over hot food.

Tips for Better Cowboy Butter

Good cowboy butter comes down to texture and balance. Keep the butter soft, keep extra moisture out, and taste before you chill it.

  • Drain the horseradish: Extra liquid can loosen the butter and make it harder to slice.
  • Grate the garlic for punch: Grated fresh garlic spreads through the butter better. Minced garlic gives you little garlic bites.
  • Use fresh herbs: Fresh parsley and fresh chives bring the pop of freshness that keeps this from tasting heavy.
  • Chill before slicing: Cold cowboy butter melts slower, which gives you that buttery topping without killing the crust on your steak.
  • Make it ahead: This is perfect for grilling nights because the butter is ready before the grill is even hot.

This compound butter is my right hand man for tritip.. 10/10 highly recommend!!!!

Cowboy Butter Variations

Once the base is mixed, you can push it hotter, smokier, brighter, or more herby without changing the whole recipe. Keep the butter ratio the same and adjust the add-ins.

  • Extra spicy: Add more cayenne or bump the red pepper flakes up to 1/2 teaspoon.
  • Milder: Skip the cayenne and use a little less horseradish.
  • More herby: Add a teaspoon of fresh thyme or dill.
  • Smokier: Add another pinch of smoked paprika.
  • Melted dipping butter: Warm a few slices in a small saucepan and use it as a cowboy sauce for shrimp, steak bites, bread, or grilled vegetables.

Cowboy Butter

No ratings yet
Prep Time: 5 minutes minutes
Servings: 8 servings
Calories: 210kcal
PDF PRINT PIN
Cowboy butter is a loaded compound butter with garlic, herbs, lemon, Dijon, a little heat, and a savory kick from Worcestershire, perfect compound butter for any grilling dish!!!

Ingredients
 

Ingredients

  • 1 cup unsalted butter softened (2 sticks)
  • 2 tbsp prepared horseradish drained if watery
  • 2 tbsp fresh parsley finely chopped
  • 1 tbsp fresh chives finely chopped
  • 1 tbsp Dijon mustard
  • 1 tbsp lemon juice
  • 1 tsp lemon zest
  • 2 cloves garlic minced or grated
  • 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce
  • 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
  • 1/2 tsp kosher salt
  • 1/4 tsp black pepper
  • 1/4 tsp crushed red pepper flakes
  • cayenne pepper optional if you want more heat

Instructions

Prevent your screen from going dark
  • Let the butter sit at room temperature until it is soft enough to mash with a fork, but not melted.
  • Add the softened butter to a bowl with the prepared horseradish, parsley, chives, Dijon, lemon juice, lemon zest, garlic, Worcestershire, smoked paprika, salt, pepper, red pepper flakes, and cayenne if using.
  • Mix everything together with a fork or rubber spatula until the herbs and seasonings are evenly distributed through the butter. Scrape the sides of the bowl so there are no plain butter pockets.
  • Taste a small amount and adjust if needed: more salt for depth, more lemon for brightness, more red pepper flakes or cayenne for heat, or a little extra horseradish if you want it sharper.
  • Spoon the butter onto a sheet of parchment paper or plastic wrap. Roll it into a log, twist the ends, and chill until firm, about 1 hour.
  • Slice into rounds and place over hot steak, burgers, grilled chicken, pork chops, vegetables, potatoes, or bread so the butter melts into the food.

Cowboy Butter FAQ

What is cowboy butter made of?

Cowboy butter is made with softened butter, fresh herbs, garlic, Dijon mustard, lemon juice, lemon zest, Worcestershire sauce, smoked paprika, black pepper, red pepper flakes, and salt. This version adds prepared horseradish for a sharper steakhouse bite.

Can I make cowboy butter ahead of time?

Yes! Cowboy butter is better when you make it ahead because it has time to firm up and slice clean. Mix it, roll it in parchment paper or plastic wrap, and refrigerate until you’re ready for steak, burgers, chicken, or vegetables.

How long does cowboy butter last in the fridge?

Cowboy butter keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 1 week. Keep it wrapped tight so it doesn’t pick up fridge smells, then slice off what you need when dinner hits the grill.

Can you freeze cowboy butter?

Yes, you can freeze cowboy butter. Wrap the log tightly, place it in a freezer-safe container, and freeze it for up to 3 months. Thaw it in the fridge, then slice and use it like fresh compound butter.

What do you put cowboy butter on?

Put cowboy butter on hot steak, burgers, grilled chicken, pork chops, potatoes, corn, vegetables, or fresh bread. A little goes a long way, especially when it melts into richer steaks or grilled meat right before serving.
